chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from Fudayl ibn Sakkarah, who said:
I entered upon Abī 'Abdillāh (عليه السلام), and he said: "O Fudayl, do you know in what thing I was looking just a little before?" He said: I said, "No."

He said: "I was looking in the Book of Fatimah (عليها السلام). There is no king who rules the earth except that he is written in it by his name and the name of his father, and I did not find anything in it for the offspring of al-Hasan."

key_terms.كِتَابِ فَاطِمَةَ: The Book of Fatimah (عليها السلام), a text associated with divinely conveyed knowledge in Shia tradition.
key_terms.مَكْتُوبٌ: Recorded or written down in the book.
key_terms.مَلِكٍ: A king or ruler exercising dominion over the earth.
key_terms.وُلْدِ الْحَسَنِ: The descendants or offspring of al-Hasan (عليه السلام).
key_terms.يَمْلِكُ الْأَرْضَ: Rules the earth; holds worldly sovereignty.

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith about the Book of Fatimah (عليها السلام) say regarding future rulers?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) was examining the Book of Fatimah (عليها السلام), described here as containing the names of earthly rulers. He states that he did not find anything therein concerning the rule of the descendants of al-Hasan, indicating a source of divinely conveyed knowledge associated with the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام).
